body.en: A *stack* is a LIFO (last in, first out) structure. With an array arr of size cap and an index top (−1 when empty): push(x) checks for overflow (top == cap − 1), then arr[++top] = x; pop() checks for underflow (top == −1), then returns arr[top−−]; peek() returns arr[top] without removing it. Stacks are used for undo, the call stack, reversing and evaluating postfix expressions.

say.en: A stack is a LIFO (last in, first out) structure. With an array arr of size cap and an index top minus 1 when empty: pushx checks for overflow (top == cap minus 1), then arr[ plus plus top] = x; pop() checks for underflow (top == minus 1), then returns arr[top--]; peek() returns arr[top] without removing it. Stacks are used for undo, the call stack, reversing and evaluating postfix expressions. LIFO; top equals minus 1 when empty.

body.en: A queue is FIFO (first in, first out): elements are added at the rear and removed from the front. In a linear array queue, front and rear only move right, so space is wasted; a *circular queue* reuses cells with % cap. A deque (double-ended queue) allows insertion and deletion at both ends: addFront, addRear, deleteFront, deleteRear. An input-restricted deque allows insertion at one end only; an output-restricted deque allows deletion at one end only. A deque can act as both a stack and a queue.

myth.en: A circular queue is full when rear == cap − 1, as in a linear queue.

truth.en: A circular queue is full when (rear + 1) % cap == front. rear can be at any index, including below front. The linear-queue test is learned first and looks the same. But after wrapping, rear = cap − 1 can happen with free cells at the front, and rear = 0 can happen in a full queue, as in the trace above.

say.en: Circular queue: rear = (rear + 1) % cap; full when (rear + 1) % cap == front.
When the last element leaves a circular queue, reset front = rear = −1.
Deque: insert and delete at both ends; input- and output-restricted forms exist.

Code written against an interface works with any implementing class.

say.en: Write the push and pop methods of a class Stack with int[] arr, int top and int cap.
void pushint x {.
if (top == cap minus 1) { System.out.println("Stack overflow"); return; }.
arr[ plus plus top] = x.
int pop() {.
if (top == minus 1) { System.out.println("Stack underflow"); return minus 9999; }.
return arr[top--].
So the answer is push guards against overflow, pop against underflow (returning minus 9999 as a signal).

body.en: In a circular queue, every index that moves forward is written (i + 1) % cap. When i is the last cell, the % brings it back to 0.
